questions.question: AC is the diameter of the circle. B is a point on the circumference. If angle BAC is 40°, then what is angle BCA?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AC is the diameter of the circle.

∠BAC = 40°

**Concept used:**

By the properties of a circle, an angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is a right angle. Therefore, ∠ABC = 90°.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/628a27e6a020534612667759d0967eeb29679aacb782336d121e157fffb83f3b.png] 

In triangle ABC, the sum of angles in a triangle is 180°. We can use this property to find ∠ABC.

So, ∠BCA = 180° - ∠BAC - ∠ABC

∠BCA = 180° - 40° - 90°

∠BCA = 50°

**Therefore, ∠BCA = 50°.**

questions.question: PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre O. PT is a tangent touching the circle at P. The secant QT intersects the circle at S. O and S are joined. If ∠SOP = 104°, what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠PTQ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

PQ is the diameter of a circle with centre O. PT is a tangent touching the circle at P. The secant QT intersects the circle at S. O and S are joined. If ∠SOP = 104º, what is the measure (in degrees) of ∠PTQ?

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c581ff64ab215cb3b068be69bcc671b3ba604eb6825f6cdfedce02e422b4d04b.png] 

∠OQS = ∠OSQ Since, (OS = OQ (radius)

But ∠SOP = ∠OQS + ∠OSQ (Exterior angle theorem)

104° = 2 ∠OQS

∠OQS = 52°

In Tringle QPT

∠PTQ = 180° - ∠OQS - ∠QPT

∠PTQ = 180°- 52° - 90°

∠PTQ = 38°

Therefore, ∠PTQ = 38°

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point A, where P and Q are points on the circle. If AP = 12 cm and ∠PAQ = 60°, then the length of chord PQ is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AP = 12 cm

∠PAQ = 60°

**Formula:**

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

sin A = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse

tan A = Perpendicular/Base

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d564c42e8d36907b7d4ad7e50a8ea5916923b385cf13244eb628480236f4281f.png] 

In OPAQ

∠OPA + ∠OQA + ∠PAQ + ∠POQ = 360°

⇒ 90° + 90° + 60° + ∠POQ = 360° - 240°

⇒ ∠POQ = 120°

⇒ ∠POA = ∠QOA = ∠POQ/2

⇒ ∠POA = 120°/2

⇒ ∠POA = 60°

In ΔOPA

tan 60 = PA/OP

⇒ √3 = 12/OP

⇒ OP = 12/√3

⇒ OP = 4√3

In ΔOPM

sin 60 = PM/OP

⇒ √3/2 = PM/4√3

⇒ PM = (√3/2) 4√3

PM = 6

⇒ PQ = 2PM

⇒ PQ = 2 × 6

⇒ PQ = 12 cm

**∴ The length of chord PQ is 12 cm.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

PX is a tangent drawn from point X.

O is the centre of the circle.

Radius of this circle is 10 cm and OX = 26 cm.

**Concept Used:**

When a tangent is drawn from an external point to a circle, it forms a right angle with the radius drawn to the point of tangency.

Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6ee89817c09fc0578f923eafdd8cdd8eef34a8343800d5abe4a7c72a518ea676.png] 

Here PX is the tangent makes 90° angle with the radius.

In triangle OPX,

OP = 10 cm

OX = 26 cm

Apply Pythagoras theorem

Hypotenuse2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

262 = 102 + Perpendicular2

Perpendicular² = 262 - 102 

Perpendicular2 = 676 - 100

Perpendicular2 = 576

Perpendicular = 24 cm

PX = 24 cm

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Two circles of radii 18 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. Then what is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The Radii of the two circles are 18 cm and 12 cm.

The length of their common chord is 16 cm.

**Concept used:**

A line that is drawn perpendicular to the chord from the center of a circle always bisects the chord.

H² = B² + P²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91913594aa8fb525717bcc6cc8c7bef2131e66d3cf8782429636be650191b2d3.png] 

At first join O, P and A 

Now, OBA is a right angle triangle and PBA is also a right angle triangle.

Length of AB = AC/2 = 16/2 = 8 cm.

Again, OB² = 18² – 8² = 260

⇒ OB = √260 = 2√65 

And BP² = 12² – 8² = 80

⇒ BP = 4√5

Now distance between their centres is OP = OB + BP

⇒ OP = 2√65 + 4√5

⇒ OP = 2√5(2 + √13)

**∴ Distance (in cm) between their centers is 2√5(2 + √13)**

questions.question: If angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 55 degree, then what will be the angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle?
questions.solution:
Given:

The angle subtended by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 55 degrees.

Concept used:

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d1c05989f2a0fa189db04629cea60370d1cee997bed9ae58452c4c12110f967d.png] 

Let O, R, and PQ be the centre, a point on the major arc, and the aforementioned chord respectively.

So, the major arc for the PQ chord is PRQ.

Hence, ∠PRQ = 55°

Here, ∠POQ is the angle subtended by the same chord, PQ on the centre of the circle.

According to the concept,

∠POQ = 2 × ∠PRQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 55°

⇒ ∠POQ = 110°

**∴ The angle subtended by the same chord on the centre of the circle is 110°.**

OB = OD = 5 √13 cm

AB = 12 cm, CD = 20 cm, AM = MB = 12/2 = 6 cm and CN = ND = 20/2 = 10 cm

In Δ MBO

OB2 = MB2 + MO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 62 + OM2

⇒ OM2 = 325 – 36 = 289

⇒ OM = √289 = 17

In Δ NDO

OD2 = ND2 + NO2

⇒ (5 √13)2 = 102 + NO2

⇒ ON2 = 325 – 100 = 225

ON = √225 = 15

As we know,

OM = MN + ON

⇒ 17 = MN + 15

⇒ MN = 17 – 15 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: Radii of two circles are 20 cm and 4 cm. Length of direct common tangent is 30 cm. What is the distance between their centres?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radii of two circles are 20 cm and 4 cm. Length of direct common tangent is 30 cm.

Length of the direct common tangent of two circles = sqrt {D² - (r₁ - r₂)²} (D = Distance between their centres, r1 = radius of the bigger circle, and r2 = radius of the smaller

Let the distance between their centres be x cm.

According to the formula,

⇒ 30 =. sqrt {x² - (20 - 4)²}

⇒ x² = 900 + 256 = 1156

⇒ x = 34
